Hazi Abul Kashem (Md) and others ----- Appellants
Vs
Janata Bank Ltd. and others ------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, CJ: Respondent No. 1 Janata Bank Limited, instituting TS No. 244 of 1998 before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka for realization of defaulted loan, got preliminary decree on 3-6-1999 which was made final on 26-9-1999. Thereafter, the Bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 18 of 2000 for realization of decreetal dues and in the said execution proceeding the appellant 1-laji Md Abul Kashem and others initially filed an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure for getting release of the property attached in the said execution case. Thereafter, by amending the said application, the same was converted to an application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 31 of 2001. 

 2. In their application under Order XXI, rule 90, the appellant, inter alma, stated that one Maliha Haque had acquired 0.33 acre of land from Khorshed Ali and others by registered deed of gift dated 24-6-1966. Out of 0.33 acre of land, Maliha Haque got physical possession in respect of 0.28 acre. Rest 0.05 acre was acquired for a road. Maliha Haque transferred some lands to Harun-or-Rashid by registered deed dated 27-3-1973. She also transferred 0.11 acre land to Md Shah Alam on 27-3-1973 and 3-4-1973 by registered deeds. Maliha Haque also transferred 0.11 acre of land to Shahidullah on 27-3-1973 and 3-4-1973. Harun-or-Rashid had transferred his land to Abdul Quayum and Nazrul Islam by registered deed dated 28-6-1987. The appellant Nos. 1 and 4, on 22-11-2000, purchased 0.0619 acre of land from Md Shah Alam. The appellant Nos. 2 and 3 purchased 0.0274 acre of land from Abdul Qayum and Md Nazrul Islam by kabala dated 1-3-2000. That is, the appellants, in total, purchased 0.0893 acre of land. Since purchase, they have been possessing the said land by constructing semi pucca tin-shed. Though Shahidullah, Shah Alam and Harun-or-Rashid purchased 0.33 acre of land from Maliha Haque they got possession in respect of 0.28 acre of land. Shahidullah got possession of 0.0935 acre of his purchased 0.11 acre of land of plot Nos. 465 and 466 from the northeast corner of the said plot. By way of amicable partition, Shahidullah and other purchasers, namely, Shah Alam, Abdul Quayum and Nazrul Islam got possession of 0.0935 acre of land from southern side. Shah Alam delivered possession of 0.0893 acre of land to the appellants from southwest portion of the plot with specific boundary. Respondent No. 5, Md Shahidullah Mia, took loan from Janata Bank by mortgaging his 0.11 acre of land. For non-payment of loan, the Bank instituted suit against respondent Nos. 2-9 and got decree. The decree holder Bank published a notification in "The Daily Ittefaq" on 18-9-2001 for selling the said property in auction for realization of the loan amount. The appellants found that the boundary of land mentioned in the schedule to the notification attracts the appellants' land though the respondent No. 5 had/has no right, title and possession over the said property. Respondent No. 5 got possession on the north-east corner of 0.28 acre of land. Shahidullah Mia had transferred 11/4 kathas land through registered deed dated 28-6-1987 to Khandaker Enayet Hossain and delivered possession thereof. Shahidullah Mia transferred 11/4 kathas and 2 3/4 kathas of land by registered deeds dated 13-8-1997. He also sold 1 katha by registered deed dated 22-1-1998 to Nobi Hossain and his son Newaj Md Hossain. Thus, Shahidullah Miah transferred his entire 0.0935 acre of land and delivered possession to them from north-east portion of the disputed plot. When it came to the notice of Nabi Hossain and others that Shahidullah Miah mortgaged the said property to the respondent No. 1 Bank, they transferred the same through registered deed dated 13-3-2000 and deed No. 437 dated 8-2-2000 to Sikder Creation Group Ltd (respondent No. 10) and delivered possession. At present Sikder Creation Group has been possessing the said land. The vendor of respondent No. 10 Nabi Hossain and Newaz Mohammad Hossain instituted Title Suit No. 40 of 2002 challenging the deed No. 3327 dated 13-8-1997 executed and registered by Md Shahidullah Mia and in the said suit respondent No. 10 was impleaded as defendant No.5 who filed written statement. Shahidullah Mia mortgaged the said property fraudulently by changing the boundary of the suit property which attracts the appellants' land. When it was notified in the daily newspaper for selling mortgaged property in auction the appellants filed an application in the execution case for staying the further proceeding of the same. The Executing Court, by order dated 25-1-2003, rejected the same. The respondent No. 10 participated in the auction and purchased the appellants' property. Against the said order dated 25-1-2003 of the learned Artha Rin Adalat the appellants filed Civil Revision in the High Court Division and the High Court Division in Civil Order No. 1146 of 2003 stayed the further proceeding of the execution case but before receiving the said order of stay by the Executing Court, the auction was held. Respondent No. 10, Sikder Creation Group tried to take delivery of possession of the appellants' land as auction purchaser through Court. The boundary of the land sold in auction should be ascertained and the property of the appellants should be released. 

 3. The respondent No. 1, Janata Bank filed written objection contending that the owners of the land of CS and SA plot Nos. 465 and 466 were Khorshed Ali and others who transferred 0.33 acre of land to Maliha Haque by registered deed dated 24-8-1967. Maliha Haque, thereafter, transferred the suit property to Shahidullah Mia and others by registered deeds dated 3-4-1973 and dated 27-3-1973 and delivered possession to them. Shahidullah Mia got possession of his purchased 0.11 acre of land from aforesaid two plots. He mortgaged the suit property to the respondent No. 1 bank against his loan. The Bank, being satisfied as to the ownership of Shahidullah Mia, granted loan. She got possession of entire 0.33 acre of land. Since Shahidullah Mia failed to repay the loan, the bank, instituting suit against him, got decree. In execution of the decree, the property of Shahidullah Mia was sold in auction. It is not correct that Shahidullah Mia fraudulently mortgaged the property to the Bank mentioning wrong boundary of his land. The claim of the appellants that the mortgaged land attracts the appellants' land is not correct. If the schedule of land described to the original mortgaged deed and the schedule of the land of the execution case and notification of auction are compared with it would be clear that there is no mistake m the boundary of the land sold in auction. The appellants, in collusion with others, creating some deeds with an object to obstruct the execution of the decree has brought such false application. The appellants cannot get any relief in his Miscellaneous Case. 

 4. The Artha Rin Adalat rejected the said application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Then the appellants preferred Miscellaneous Appeal in the High Court Division which was dismissed. Then they filed review petition in the High Court Division which was also rejected by the impugned order. 

 8. It appears from the materials on record that the instant appeal has been preferred against the judgment and order passed in Civil Rule No. 878 (Review) (FM) 2013 which was filed against the judgment and order passed in FMA No. 37 of 2011. It is settled principle that the review petition may be entertainable only in case of discovery of new and important matter for evidence which, after exercise due diligence, was not within the knowledge of the review petitioner or could not be produced by him at the time when order was made or on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of record or for any other sufficient reason. 

 9. It appears that the High Court Division observed that the instant application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not entertainable and that the remedy of the third party applicant lies under section 32 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which provides the provision that the third party claimant is required to furnish 10% security on the decreetal amount for getting release of the property attached in connection with Artha Rin Execution Case. In case of failure to furnish such security the application would not be entertainable by the Artha Rin Adalat in execution proceeding in view of the specific provision as contemplated under section 32 of the AM which is a special law. In the instant case, the third party claimant, igno-ring the said provision provided in the Ain, has filed the instant application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 10. It is relevant hereto mention that section 6 of the Ain, specifically provides that the application of the provision regarding execution of money decree under the Code of Civil Procedure is subject to the provisions of the Ain. The provision of the code of Civil Procedure will be applicable to the matters of execution of decree of the Adalat which are not inconsistent with the provisions of the Ain. Section 32 of the AM specifically provides to get release the attached property of third party claimant in a execution proceeding upon depositing 10% of decreetal dues as security and to ventilate the grievance. The appellants initially filed application under section 32 of the Ain but the same was converted to an application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code which provides the provision of setting aside auction on the ground of material irregularity or fraud in holding auction. Within four corners of their, application, the appellants did not state anything about the material irregularity and fraud in holding auction. We are of the view that the instant application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not at all entertainable since the appellants in their application have failed to make out a case of material irregularity and fraud in holding auction.
